title: Manchester United's players, not Michael Carrick, should shoulder the blame after embarrassing loss to Chelsea - CBS Sports

body:
Senior players have complained about tactics and recruitment, but a self-inflicted collapse at Chelsea showed the squad only has itself to blame
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LONDON -- Manchester United players have been at great pains in recent weeks to point out how they have been failed by the powers that be, by those with supposedly more influence than the 11 lads on the field. On occasion, you could argue they had the measure of the situation. There's just one little note for Lisandro Martinez, Bruno Fernandes and anyone else who counts themselves among the Old Trafford mutineers.If you're going to start demanding greater professional standards from your employers, you would be well advised to hold yourself to the same level. It would be a real problem if, for instance, you earned yourself two yellow cards in the space of 210 seconds, handing your opponents the penalty from which they win the game. Sympathy will be in quite short supply for those who complain about the head coach's tactics or the sporting director's recruitment but then, when the circumstances are right, fail to exploit prime opportunities.Lisandro Martinez was right when he intimated a fortnight ago that Jason Wilcox had bungled recruitment this summer, an assessment that seemed to be supported by Amad Diallo. Bruno Fernandes had a point in Como. Michael Carrick had picked the wrong tactics for the occasion. One of the most significant problems at Old Trafford is that the wrong executives, appointed by the wrong owners, are not exploiting the financial heft that United, even loaded with debt, still have. Another is that Carrick is not a good enough coach to paper over the cracks.Those weren't the problems at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. This was a game lost for United by senior players. Fernandes and Amad, who is now 24 and has played over 100 games for the club, partly number among them. It is rarely wise to over-index on anyone missing chances; perhaps only Amad's last shot of the first half could reasonably have been termed one he should have scored. Then again, if you've got notes about tactics, you had best exploit the mismatches that come your way.
Whether through Chelsea's early disorganization or Carrick's adjustments -- which included center forward Bryan Mbeumo peeling off to the right and taking center backs with him -- Amad and Fernandes were afforded space and time to excel. Had they exploited them in the first half, United would have been firmly in the ascendancy. 
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Perhaps United heads would have melted anyway. It does not seem to take much to unleash a chain reaction of mental anguish on this team. One clumsy error begets two or three more, typified by Morgan Rogers' opener. Thirty percent individual brilliance, his clipped finish was as much a function of no one defending the space he was running into. Peter Bankes had the best view of proceedings as Andrey Santos went steaming in on fresh air."When you concede a goal it's never a good goal to concede. Morgan went through the middle of us. The game was in the balance, and to concede like that was," said Carrick, pausing as if catching himself before he said something he regretted. "Yeah it was a big moment for sure. I'm just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now."
From there the task fell to Martinez to escort Chelsea across the finishing line. An arm on the midriff was not enough to slow Rogers' advance, so the next time their paths crossed, the Argentine went altogether more physical, rugby-tackling the attacker as he was making his way away from goal. It wasn't just that it was a clear yellow-card tackle; Martinez didn't even stop the attack.It took two more hacks from Martinez and Diogo Dalot before the ball ran away from Rogers. The resulting free kick was cleared for a corner, at which the man they call The Butcher thought it was wiser to start carving up Wesley Fofana than defend the delivery into the box. 
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Martinez was the most obvious culprit, but right across the field United flatlined the moment Chelsea scored their first. Even the 13 minutes between Rogers' goal and the contest effectively ending with a Cole Palmer penalty saw a string of players lose the run of themselves. Carlos Baleba had hardly excelled beforehand, but passes he was clipping with a pitching wedge before were now being smacked around with a driver. United could not pass their way out of the pressure that Chelsea applied to them in their own half. Free kicks flew to no one in particular, although perhaps it shouldn't have been surprising that no one was connecting with balls in the air when all their heads were on Mars.
What follows will be the usual psychodrama of Manchester United, all the more so if results go against them and they find themselves in the bottom three at the end of the weekend. At the time Carrick was asked about it, that was the position United occupied, with Nottingham Forest drawing at Brentford. "You've got to keep moving forward and winning games, it's as simple as that. There's no words that make it any different. You've got to move forward and win football matches, it's as simple as that."It does not look simple. Their nine-game winless run is United's longest since 1988. With games against Roma and Aston Villa to come, double figures seems a real risk. Carrick confirmed he will be in charge for the first of those games on Tuesday night, but the two-week sacking window that is a November international break looms large. And yet, if the United hierarchy has backed its manager after he did bungle the tactics against Como, how could his sacking be justified when his players took events out of the coach's control?Carrick certainly had the backing of the traveling fans, who went through the full repertoire of chants against the Glazers, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Wilcox and the new stadium. All those grievances are well merited, but this was only a game lost by the executives in the sense that they should long ago have dispensed with some of the underperformers, with or without the offer of a transfer fee. 
There will be the next round of the familiar debates on ownership and on how long Carrick might last. All of those will start from what these players did wrong. They are a constant through line in the perma-crisis, garlanded with individual awards, bedecked with honors for their international side and chronically incapable of delivering to the standards that they demand of others at United.

title: How can Thunder survive Chet Holmgren injury? Rookie becomes vital, trade rumors swirl - CBS Sports
description: As a third star will miss significant time due to injury, the Thunder face a challenging road ahead
body:
As a third star will miss significant time due to injury, the Thunder face a challenging road ahead
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Oklahoma City Thunder announced that Chet Holmgren underwent treatment on Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear in his right knee, an issue that will keep him out of the lineup for the next 8-10 weeks. With Jalen Williams out for the season following a gruesome leg injury and Cason Wallace set to miss most of the season after surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder, the Thunder are now without three of their top six players on the roster less than a month into the season. The Thunder are off to a 4-1 start so far, but a lopsided loss to the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday night with Holmgren out offered a glimpse into how challenging life will be with another star on the shelf. 
        
            
                What Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace injuries mean for the Thunder and why a trade isn't so simple
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
For a team that began the season as the co-favorites in the Western Conference alongside the San Antonio Spurs with a win total over 60, now they face a challenge maintaining a spot in the top four in the West after losing so much of their expected production two weeks into the season. 
Oklahoma City has been dominant in recent seasons largely due to its tremendous depth, but this summer saw them take the first steps in shedding that due to the perils of the second apron and rising costs of keeping a talented young core together. Gone are three established contributors in Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe, and while those were understandable cost-cutting measures, they exacerbate the challenge of dealing with serious injuries to key players at all three levels of the floor. If there's a silver lining, it's that Holmgren's injury will only cost him a couple of months. But with Wallace and Williams out, losing one of the league's best rim protectors will be extremely difficult to deal with. This was already going to be a challenging season for coach Mark Daigneault without two key backcourt stars, but now he has to shuffle his lineups across the board with Holmgren out. Time to sink or swim for Aday MaraThe Thunder probably hoped to bring their rookie big man along slowly, but with Holmgren out, the 7-foot-3 center out of Michigan will have to take on a larger spot in the rotation. Mara impressed in spot duty in his debut against Victor Wembanyama on opening night, showing why the Thunder drafted him to combat their chief rival with a rare player with the size and length to bother him -- and alleviate the stress Holmgren faces dealing with Wemby. 
Mara then picked up his first double-double in a win over the Phoenix Suns on Monday, as he got his first extended burn with Holmgren out, scoring 11 points and pulling down 10 boards in 20 minutes. He was less effective in 21 minutes against the Mavs, and the Thunder will have to navigate the ups and downs of the rookie experience as Mara gets more comfortable in his expanded role. 
Offensively, Mara is a play-finisher at the rim. So far this season, 80% of his field goal attempts have come within four feet of the rim and 75% of his attempts have come off of zero dribbles. With Mara on the floor, the offense has to adjust compared to what they can do with the rest of their center rotation. Where Isaiah Hartenstein can be a high post hub and Holmgren and Jaylin Williams can space the floor, Mara has less variability to his game. That doesn't mean he can't be effective, but it does require an adjustment on Oklahoma City's end to put him in the right spots and find ways to still create space for others when he's on the floor. On defense, Mara gives them a needed rim protector and he's proven to be a high-caliber shot blocker already with seven blocks in five games despite relatively light minutes. However, like many young shot blockers, Mara is learning to navigate an increased minutes load without fouling. He has picked up nine fouls combined in his two games with 20-plus minutes. Defense will be Mara's calling card, and over the next two months, the Thunder will hope to see him continue learning to be impactful without fouling to maximize his time on the floor. 
The Thunder never viewed this season as one to focus on development, but at this point they have little choice but to embrace that with Mara. He has the potential to be a key contributor to this team and play an extremely valuable role as they get set for a decade-long battle with the Wemby-led Spurs. With Holmgren out, he's going to get far more extended opportunities to see the floor than expected early in his rookie year, and perhaps that can pay dividends down the road for Oklahoma City. Will this change OKC's approach to the trade market?With Williams out for the year and Wallace out for at least most of it, there were plenty of rumblings about the Thunder exploring their options on the trade market. A deal was unlikely to happen until at least December 15, when players who signed this summer become available, but Oklahoma City figured to spend the next month-plus evaluating its roster and keeping an eye on potential additions from around the league to stay in the contender realm. With Holmgren out, one wonders whether that changes the calculus for Sam Presti -- or at least the timeline for making a move. Holmgren is expected to return in January, which would allow the Thunder to wait until he's back and see how he's performing coming off of the knee procedure for a couple of weeks before the trade deadline. 

        
            
                Five ways the NBA's injury outbreak could impact trade season: OKC has work to do, Rockets are in control
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Thunder should be able to manage two-plus months of a center rotation of Hartenstein, Williams and Mara -- with more Kenrich Williams at the four as well -- meaning their focus will still be on adding on the wing and in the backcourt. Presti may want to see exactly what he has this season before making a significant in-season move. The Thunder could try to weather the storm with the roster they have until Holmgren returns and see where they are in the West before determining whether to make a smaller move or a more foundation-shaking trade. Could Shai Gilgeous-Alexander win a third-straight MVP?No one has won three straight MVPs since Larry Bird in the 80s. For one, it's hard to maintain that level for three straight seasons, but as we've seen over the years, even when the greats do stay in the MVP conversation, voter fatigue typically sets in after a player wins two and voters seek out someone else.
However, with the injuries piling up in Oklahoma City, if there were ever a year for a player to break that drought and become the first to three-peat as MVP in 40 years, it could be Shai Gilgeous-Alexander dragging this Thunder team to another top-four seed with such a depleted roster. It's been a relatively slow start to the season for Gilgeous-Alexander, averaging 26.0 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game on 45.9/26.5/87.5 shooting splits. That kind of production obviously won't get him a third MVP award, but if he ups his level and carries this Thunder squad without Holmgren for half the season and without Williams and Wallace for most of it, he will have to garner real consideration. 
        
            
                NBA's 'unprecedented' early season injury crisis has players and coaches searching for answers
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Some of his candidacy will be determined by who else is in the mix early on -- Luka Dončić seems poised to put up massive numbers in L.A. -- but the circumstances in Oklahoma City this season are so unique that Gilgeous-Alexander could break the run of back-to-back MVPs who have fallen short in pursuit of a third straight. 
Gilgeous-Alexander's play will determine exactly how the Thunder proceed this season. If he plays at his typical MVP level and the Thunder look like a threat, Presti may have no choice but to try and make a splash ahead of the deadline to bring in reinforcements to chase a second championship. If it's a down year for Gilgeous-Alexander without some of his top support elements around him, perhaps there's less of a push to go all-in this season and Oklahoma City could look to ride out the storm and hope for better health in 2027-28.

        The Packers' defense has turned the corner this season, and now, reinforcements could be on the way. It's not just any reinforcements, either. It's All-Pro reinforcements. Micah Parsons and Green Bay are targeting a Thanksgiving Eve return against the Rams for the star pass rusher, per NFL Network. He has not played since Week 15 of last season, when he tore his ACL and meniscus against the Broncos.According to the report, Parsons is slated to return to practice this coming week (Green Bay already won this week, beating the Panthers 27-19 to move to 5-3) and participate in individual drills ahead of Week 9. If all goes to plan, he will progress to team drills ahead of Week 10. The Packers have a Week 11 bye and then face the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25.Should Parsons return then, it would be nearly a year since he originally suffered the injury and nearly 11 months since he had surgery, which featured an ACL reconstruction and a full repair of his meniscus.
Parsons was his normal superstar self after arriving from the Cowboys via a blockbuster trade last year, racking up 12.5 sacks in 14 games despite changing teams days before the season opener. The Packers ranked fifth in yards per play allowed through 15 weeks last year. From Week 16 onward, after Parsons' injury, they were 26th. Their season came to an unceremonious end with a loss to the Bears in the Wild Card Round.Early on, it looked like the Packers were on pace for a similarly poor defensive performance without their star edge rusher. But Jonathan Gannon's unit has improved significantly over the course of the season. Since Week 4, Green Bay is third in yards per play allowed and has an NFL-high 13 turnovers forced.
Adding Parsons to the mix will be a huge boost in the uber-competitive NFC North and for the playoff push in general. Despite a 5-3 record, Green Bay is last in the division. SportsLine currently gives the Packers a 61% chance to make the postseason.

title: Can Jeremiah Smith's Heisman Trophy candidacy survive Ohio State's QB shuffle? - CBS Sports
description: With Ohio State turning to an inexperienced quarterback, the Buckeyes' star receiver must keep producing to fend
body:
With Ohio State turning to an inexperienced quarterback, the Buckeyes' star receiver must keep producing to fend off rising Heisman challengers
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:51 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Jeremiah Smith is the Heisman Trophy favorite at every sportsbook entering Week 9 thanks to a sensational start to the season that saw him climb to the top of most all-time Big Ten receiving lists. Smith has 52 catches for 984 yards and 12 touchdowns in seven games this season, only trailing Oregon State freshman sensation Jesse Legree in yards and touchdowns nationally, and is carrying the Ohio State passing offense. Smith accounts for 43.5% of the Buckeyes' receiving yards and 54.5% of their receiving touchdowns this season, despite being the central focus of every Ohio State opponent's game plan. With most of the top quarterbacks around the country struggling in a chaotic 2026 season, Smith has asserted himself as the nation's best player through the midpoint of the schedule. The challenge for Smith will be holding onto that position as the Heisman favorite to collect college football's most prestigious trophy in December. The fast-charging Miami duo of Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney -- who face their own challenge in splitting votes as teammates -- present one problem for Smith's pursuit of the Heisman, but the biggest determining factor in whether Smith wins the award will be how Ohio State's sudden quarterback uncertainty impacts his production. 
Julian Sayin was not shy about targeting Smith early and often, regardless of the coverage the star receiver faced, but Sayin may be done for the season after suffering an injury late against Indiana. Ryan Day has yet to announce whether freshman Luke Fahey or sophomore Tavien St. Clair will get the starting nod against USC -- or whether both quarterbacks will play -- but in either case they'll be thrown into the fire as young, unproven quarterbacks tasked with keeping Ohio State as a national title contender. Whether it's Fahey, St. Clair or a combination of the two, Smith will need to maintain his incredible pace with a new quarterback throwing him the ball. The question is whether Ohio State's QB situation will help or hurt Smith's Heisman case over the final five games, and there are reasonable arguments on both sides. 
        
            
                College Football Power Rankings: Ohio State remains No. 1 over Miami as chaos creates shakeup elsewhere
                
                    Brandon Marcello                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
How Smith can lose the HeismanThere are two schools of thought for how this will impact Smith, and we'll start with the negative. A new quarterback will not have the same rhythm with Smith as Sayin, who has been throwing Smith the ball for two years and went through an entire offseason getting all of the first-team reps as the unquestioned starter. 
The connection between Sayin and Smith was obvious from the jump to start this season, and Sayin had complete and total trust and confidence in Smith -- even in situations where the coverage was there. A young quarterback will likely be tasked with steering the ship and managing the offense, especially considering Ohio State has an elite defense once again. A more conservative offensive approach from Ryan Day could mean fewer targets for Smith, especially down the field, and if he's more limited while Miami's star duo continue to tear it up for the Hurricanes, Smith could get passed over. There's also the possibility of even more instability if Ohio State goes with a two-quarterback system, which makes it even tougher for Smith to establish a rhythm with either. If Fahey and St. Clair are splitting series, that only increases the degree of difficulty for Smith, as he has to adjust to the timing of two different quarterbacks. 
The concern for Smith is that his best performances could end up being four of the first five games of the season. While the Heisman is a full-season award, the human element in voting tends to place more weight on what a player does late in the season. Smith's early potential Heisman moment, 8 catches for 164 yards and a touchdown at Texas, was ruined by an Ohio State collapse to lose that game as they turtled up offensively. There aren't any more games against top-10 opponents on the schedule (Northwestern at No. 20 is the only ranked opponent currently), and with the quarterback uncertainty, Smith might miss out on that late-season game that cements his status as this year's Heisman. How Smith can win the HeismanThere is an optimistic view for Smith and those holding a Heisman ticket with his name on it. If he continues to produce at a high level, it's going to appear even more impressive after Ohio State went to a backup.
Smith won't have to average 140 yards per game to impress voters, but if he's still hanging around 100 yards and a touchdown on average each game with Fahey or St. Clair, that might be enough. It was already clear that the message in the Ohio State quarterback room was "find No. 4 and throw it to him" with Sayin, and there's an argument to be made that could be hammered home even further with a young quarterback. There's no player in the country you'd rather have as a target for an unproven quarterback, and if the Buckeyes are going to win a title, they have to establish some kind of passing threat. Telling a young QB to trust that Smith will bail them out even in tight coverage wouldn't be the worst plan in the world, and Smith is going to make them look good more often than not. While Ohio State's closing schedule is no longer as daunting as it once looked a few months ago, it still presents opportunities for major production if the Buckeyes are willing to open it up.
USC's defense remains porous, and Smith should have plenty of opportunities to produce against the Trojans' secondary, even with a QB making his first career start on the road. Oregon is a shell of what it was supposed to be, and while the Ducks have been solid on defense, it feels like a matter of time before the dam breaks if the offense remains inept. Northwestern has been one of college football's biggest surprises this year, but they get the job done with offensive creativity, and Smith will be a matchup nightmare for the Wildcats on the perimeter. Nebraska is trying to keep the wheels from falling off before the Huskers host the Buckeyes in a few weeks, while the Michigan game always seems to be a defensive struggle. There will be ample opportunity for Smith to author his Heisman moment, and even though he won't get a chance to do so against a fellow top-10 team (and unfortunately lost his best effort against a top opponent with Ohio State's collapse at Texas), his top competitors only have one chance to do so themselves. 
This year's competition might work out in Smith's favor as well. Toney and Mensah will likely split some votes, and their only chance to author a true Heisman moment that registers on a national scale will be their game on Nov. 7 against Notre Dame. If the Irish win that game or Miami's offense sputters at all for the first time this season, Smith's path will be even clearer to lifting the Heisman in December. It shouldn't take long to find out whether Smith's Heisman candidacy will take a major hit or not. Saturday's game against USC is about as friendly as Ohio State could ask for in terms of the defense they will face for a young quarterback's debut. If they aren't willing to throw the ball against the Trojans, Smith is going to be in real trouble. However, a big game will boost his credentials and solidify his position as the favorite.

Bailey is producing on the edge while Omar Cooper Jr. and Kenyon Sadiq are flashing playmaking juice, offering New York foundational pieces despite a rocky start

        Aaron Glenn's second season as head coach of the New York Jets is off to a fascinating start. The team has won two games, and four of five losses have been decided by one score. However, a Week 7 loss to the previously winless Miami Dolphins has fans once again questioning if Glenn's job security is on the line. This season's issues cannot be traced back to a singular decision, but rather a series. Will the selection of Texas Tech edge rusher David Bailey at No. 2 overall be added to the list? Are Oregon tight end Kenyon Sadiq and Indiana wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. building blocks for the offense? Let's revisit the Jets' 2026 NFL Draft selections and find out.With the No. 2 overall selection....The choice, believed to be either Ohio State linebacker Arvell Reese or Bailey, was debated publicly for months. Bailey was a more refined pass rusher, but Reese had higher upside. The latter has been playing more of an off-ball linebacker role for New York, which was always his best, most natural position. Ohio State linebacker Sonny Styles, who was drafted by the Commanders, was one other player who should have been considered in that spot, because of the total package. Through seven games, the jury is still accepting evidence in Bailey's case. He has been credited with 26 pressures and 5.5 sacks — three of which came against the Browns — by TruMedia. His 15.4% pressure rate ranks No. 11 among players with at least 150 pass rush snaps, but his 3.62 seconds to sack is below average. The numbers are reflected in the play. A portion of his production is either late in the down or comes when a quarterback steps into pressure. Bailey plays with maximum effort but would benefit from developing a rush plan rather than getting stuck on post-spin moves or swipes around the edge.   
In the run game, Bailey shows the requisite power and will occasionally stack blockers, but he also willingly loses gap integrity at times. If New York had tunnel vision on adding pass rush help with the No. 2 overall selection, they made the correct decision. It is also difficult to fault them for not considering other positions when the draft class, as a whole, was filled with outliers rather than premier physical specimens. Bailey has played 81.3% of the defensive snaps this season, so he is a full-time player already in the Big Apple. His ceiling is probably that of a high-end No. 2 pass rusher, who would benefit from the addition equivalency of a high-end NBA scorer capable of creating his own shot. Fortunately, New York has three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft to potentially attack that need. 
Help in the pass gameAfter the conclusion of the 2025 NFL season, radio stations in New York filled a lot of their airtime discussing a lack of viable contributors in the pass game. The addition of Adonai Mitchell, in combination with Garrett WIlsonWilson, was not enough. The Jets utilized selections No. 16 and 30 on Sadiq and Cooper. The franchise previously selected offensive tackles Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou in the first round. There was a run on the position after Sadiq was taken, so the only non-offensive tackles missed out on were wide receiver K.C. Concepcion, safety Dillon Thieneman, cornerback Chris Johnson and defensive tackle Peter Woods. New York traded up from No. 33 overall to select Cooper.There is an argument to be made that wide receiver Denzel Boston or linebacker Jacob Rodriguez may have been better choices than Cooper, but recent play makes that less obvious. Although he has only appeared in three games, the Indiana product has skyrocketed into the top five among rookie receivers in receiving yards with back-to-back 100+ yard performances. 
Cooper has done well attacking zone coverages but is more limited against man looks. A few of his biggest plays were the product of poor coverage communication and confusion created by a risky Geno Smith throw. His superhero qualities are his physicality and elusiveness after the catch. He is averaging 9.3 yards after the catch per reception, according to TruMedia, which is easily the highest among rookie receivers with at least 10 receptions. Zachariah Branch is No. 2 at 6.4 yards after the catch per reception. Sadiq is a bulldog in the run game. As an attached blocker, he gets after blocks like a hungry dog with a bone. In general, he looks like a tightly wound ball of energy, randomly trying to hurdle in situations that do not call for it or unnecessarily jumping for a pass. He is a natural pass catcher who also attacks zone coverage and excels at creating yards after the catch. Sadiq is third in the aforementioned statistic at 6.3 yards after the catch per reception. Long-term outlookThere is nothing to suggest New York made a bad selection with any of its three first-round selections. All have been contributors and project as such for the long term. Bailey and Cooper look more like complementary starters, whereas Sadiq has a higher ceiling at his respective position. 
Availability will be key. Cooper has been limited to three of the team's seven games. Sadiq has played in all seven games after missing most of training camp and the preseason recovering from a hernia injury. Injuries had not been a problem for Sadiq in Eugene.

        The Indianapolis Colts are open to trading running back Jonathan Taylor and are actively engaging with teams about a deal, according to ESPN and NFL Network.The news comes amid a Colts' fire sale that has seen Indianapolis (2-5) trade two cornerstones this week. The Colts traded Quenton Nelson to Seattle for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick and traded DeForest Buckner to San Francisco for a 2027 fourth-round pick.The return stands to be much bigger for Taylor. The Colts have already received at least one offer that includes a second-round pick plus additional compensation, per ESPN. Taylor, who said Thursday he's proud to wear the horseshoe and hasn't requested a trade, remains one of the league's most productive backs. He has twice led the NFL in rushing touchdowns, including last season, and led the league in rushing yards in 2021 on his way to first-team All-Pro honors. He has eight rushing touchdowns through seven games this year, putting him on pace to threaten his career high of 18.ESPN reports the teams with at least some interest include the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants and Seahawks. Here's how each could fit:
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay PackersThe Packers (5-3) recently got Josh Jacobs back from the commissioner-exempt list, but Green Bay's rushing struggles are reaching historic proportions. Green Bay is last in rushing yards per game (60.6) and yards per rush (2.9). The former is on pace to be the worst since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, the latter on pace to be the second-worst. That has put an enormous weight on quarterback Jordan Love: Currently, nearly 82% of Green Bay's yards have come via the pass, on pace for the highest rate since the merger.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York GiantsJohn Harbaugh has fiddled with New York's running back rotation this season but is on the record that he would "love" a bell cow a la Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley on his team. The Giants (4-2-1) lead a wide-open NFC East, and Taylor could not only take the load off new starter J.J. McCarthy but also be a boon; playing next to Jaxson Dart would be an enticing look next year. Cam Skattebo's bounce-back Week 7 performance after getting no touches in Week 6 might have placated previous backfield worries, but clearly New York is willing to poke around for an upgrade.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Denver BroncosThe Broncos (5-2) sent a first-round pick to Miami for Jaylen Waddle this offseason, though it hasn't really worked out yet. Would they make another big move, this time for a running back? Denver has struggled to muster much on the ground, which has only exacerbated Bo Nix's struggles. Broncos running backs rank 10th in yards before first contact per rush, suggesting good blocking, but 30th in yards after first contact per rush. Rookie Jonah Coleman has impressed but also dealt with injuries. Denver does have an extra fourth-round pick in 2027.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seattle SeahawksSeattle (4-3) already did business with Indianapolis this week, and perhaps reuniting Nelson with Taylor could be the boost their attempt for a second straight Super Bowl title needs. The Seahawks very much miss Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP, and haven't found much on the ground without him. Zach Charbonnet is on his way back, as is first-round pick Jadarian Price, but Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have both had devastating fumbles in the interim. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury was with the 49ers when they acquired Christian McCaffrey midseason, so he knows the value of a great top running back.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsThe Vikings are 6-0, but their 10 touchdowns are the fewest by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions. Minnesota has moved the ball decently but hasn't found the finishing touch to get into the end zone. Taylor has 40 touchdowns over the past three seasons, the third-most in the NFL, and pairing him with a mobile quarterback like Kyler Murray would be a treat for Kevin O'Connell. Minnesota also has draft capital to spare, including an extra third-round pick, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.

title: Revisiting Cardinals 2026 NFL Draft: Was drafting Jeremiyah Love the right choice for Arizona? - CBS Sports
description: Taking a running back at No. 3 was a luxury an incomplete roster could not afford, especially with pressing needs
body:
Taking a running back at No. 3 was a luxury an incomplete roster could not afford, especially with pressing needs in the trenches and Arizona sitting at 2-5
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        What are first-year head coach Mike LaFleur's beliefs about how to build a team and who would be those foundational players for the Arizona Cardinals? Those were the questions being asked prior to the 2026 NFL Draft. The offensive line was thought to be a priority for the offensive-minded head coach, but was there a prospect worth consideration for the No. 3 overall selection, or was best player available the more astute approach? It was not until the final month before the draft that Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love had been associated with the Cardinals. Then, the conversation evolved into: "Can the Cardinals afford to select a luxury position when there are so many other needs on the roster?" Las Vegas selected Ashton Jeanty No. 6 overall in 2025, and the team was worse the following season.   Nearly halfway through the regular season, was Arizona justified in picking a running back No. 3 overall? 
Love's impact and the opportunity costThe rookie out of Notre Dame has played in five games this season but has now missed time with a high ankle sprain.  He has been on the field for 34.4% of the offensive snaps through Week 7. In those moments, he has accumulated 67 carries for 245 yards (3.7 yards per carry) and one rushing touchdown, as well as 11 receptions for 36 yards and one touchdown through the air. Free agent acquisition Tyler Allgeier has taken on a share of the workload. At 6-feet, 212 pounds, Love is an upright runner who is patient allowing blocks to develop and following them. He displays great vision and has the skill set to be on the field for all three downs. The runner stands tall in the pocket and pops oncoming rushers but inconsistently sustains blocks and leaks out into routes. However, among running backs with at least 50 carries, Love ranks dead last in tackle avoidance rate (6.0%), according to TruMedia. Love has been a good player, and yet the Cardinals are 2-5 on the season. Saying a team in Arizona's situation should not take a running back is not a reflection of Love's talent, but of the opportunity cost. The value of his contract is fourth-highest and features the largest guarantee among running backs. By comparison, the value of Carnell Tate's contract, who was taken one pick later, ranks No. 10 among wide receivers and is second-most on his own team. 
If they had taken the highest-drafted offensive tackle (Spencer Fano) or Arvell Reese, those contracts would have been more valuable to the team and arguably more impactful on the field. The situation is comparable to Jeanty in Las Vegas last season. A running back should be the whipped cream or cherry (depending upon one's personal preference) on top for an offense. The offensive line must be sound, and the quarterback must be able to threaten downfield so that defenses are not bearing down on the box. If those roles are intact, then a team would be justified in using a high selection on the position regardless of the defense's competency. Long-term outlookIs Love one of the league's elite running backs? Maybe not, but he will be a key contributor through his rookie contract at the very least. As a draft prospect, he looked more like an improved, more patient version of Travis Etienne, but it would not be fair to put a cap on his ceiling until Arizona adequately addresses the offensive line. 
Ironically, a previous stance against running backs has softened. NFL teams have shown more willingness to extend running backs beyond the rookie contract. Running backs are also playing into their late 20s and early 30s, which has slowly eroded the longevity argument. As the run game becomes more predominant across the league, the value of the position should rise.

body:
Another Oregon football player has been booked for his role in a high-speed chase two weeks ago
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:53 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Oregon freshman wide receiver Messiah Hampton was arrested on Friday afternoon after a high-speed chase where two vehicles evaded police on Oct. 18 following the Ducks' win over Nebraska. Hampton was booked into Lane County Jail and released later on Friday evening on one felony charge of attempting to elude police and one misdemeanor of reckless driving, per jail records. One of the vehicles from the high-speed chase was abandoned near where wide receiver Evan Stewart was arrested for DUII, but Stewart is not considered a suspect in the chase and prosecutors declined to file charges against Stewart, per KATU News. Tight end Jamari Johnson was also cited for speeding that Saturday night, but police also don't consider him a suspect in the chase and are working to identify the other driver besides Hampton, per the Oregonian. 
"Mr. Hampton has been identified as the driver of one of the vehicles," Springfield Police deputy chief George Crolly said on Friday evening. "We are still working to identify the driver of the other vehicle."Hampton has 18 catches for 161 yards and two touchdowns this season, becoming a productive part of the Ducks' offense in his first season on campus. He was a late addition to Oregon's availability report for an undisclosed reason ahead of Oregon's loss to Illinois last week and appeared on Friday's availability report as "out" again. 
Hampton's arrest continues a poor season in Eugene on and off the field for Dan Lanning's squad. The 4-3 Ducks welcome No. 20 Northwestern to Autzen Stadium on Saturday, trying to stay above .500 on the season, but continue to deal with off-field distractions stemming from the aftermath of their victory over Nebraska two weeks ago.
